details: This package is a self-declared controlled test canary ("controlled npm backend ingestion"). It ships package/backend-canary.js, which issues an HTTPS GET to hxxps://webhook[.]site/314c4c8c-4eba-4012-9bf5-0a45805cd355/npm-backend-574b7ccdaeb61dd9dd70d6d4/lifecycle carrying two SHA-256 hashed query parameters: host (hash of /etc/hostname) and user (hash of the OS username). No credentials, tokens, environment values, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted — the payload is a host-metadata beacon only. The tarball contains backend-canary.js, index.js (exports the string 'controlled') and marker.txt with an NPM_BACKEND_UTF8_BOM_ marker. This package is a controlled research/probe artifact testing npm registry external-URL ingestion. Its package.json points the bugs, homepage, funding and repository fields at a webhook[.]site callback (id 314c4c8c-4eba-4012-9bf5-0a45805cd355), and it ships package/backend-canary.js plus a package/marker.txt identifier file. When backend-canary.js is executed it reads /etc/hostname and the OS username, SHA-256 hashes both, and issues an HTTPS GET to hxxps://webhook[.]site/314c4c8c-4eba-4012-9bf5-0a45805cd355/npm-backend-574b7ccdaeb61dd9dd70d6d4/lifecycle?host=<sha256>&user=<sha256>. Only host metadata is transmitted — no environment values, credentials, tokens or file contents are collected, and no install or lifecycle hook in the package invokes the script (the package main, package/index.js, is a no-op).
